# dsh -- DeepSeek Harness CLI and web UI

The DeepSeek Harness capability is split across three candies by
concern (R3):

- `dsh` — the CLI only (`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.2.0-rc.2 via npm).
- `dsh-web` — the loopback-only, token-authenticated web UI + socat
  forwarder (composes `dsh`).
- `dsh-tui` — the dsh-TUI terminal-UI plugin + its typed terminal
  channel (composes `dsh`).

## Candy Properties (dsh-web)

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Install files | `charly.yml`, `dsh-entrypoint` |
| Depends | `dsh`, `nodejs` (>=22.19.0), `supervisord` |
| Port | 3080 (web UI, loopback) / 3081 (socat forwarder) |
| Volume | `~/.dsh` (profiles + plugin data + the captured web token) |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `DSH_HOME` | `~/.dsh` |
| `DSH_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` | unset/empty by default; a space- or comma-separated list of `host:port` authorities the entrypoint forwards as repeatable `--trusted-host` (set it when the pod is reached through a reverse proxy) |

A reverse-proxy deployment (`tailscale serve`, an SSH `-L` tunnel) presents a
non-loopback Host, so without this the shell loads while every `/api/*`
call returns 403.

## Packages

RPM/DEB/PAC: `socat` (the loopback→eth0 forwarder)

## The web UI is loopback-only and token-authenticated

`dsh web` binds **127.0.0.1:3080 only**: dsh-web-app hard-rejects
`--host 0.0.0.0` (RCE safety). A container's published
port maps to the container's eth0, not loopback — so the charly-owned
`dsh-entrypoint` runs `dsh web` in the background and `exec`s a socat
forwarder (`TCP-LISTEN:3081,fork,reuseaddr TCP:127.0.0.1:3080`) that
exposes the web app on eth0. socat cannot share port 3080 (Linux
forbids a wildcard + loopback listener pair on one port), so the
published port (auto-allocated host port → container 3081) reaches
the web UI through socat. On the vm substrate the `ssh -L` forward
targets loopback directly — socat just doesn't hurt there.

## The web UI has TWO independent auth layers

`dsh web` authenticates at **two** layers, and a probe that only
checks the first will pass while the browser UI is broken:

1. **The launch token.** Each process mints a random token and prints
   its readiness URL as `dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...`.
   There is no flag or config that disables it. `GET /?token=…` on the
   **root only** answers `303` and sets a signed, authority-bound,
   `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie whose authority is the *request
   Host* — so it follows the proxy authority rather than staying
   `127.0.0.1`. A missing or wrong-authority cookie returns **401**.

2. **The Host / Origin browser-trust fence** (`dsh-client-connection`'s
   `api-request-trust`), which every API and WebSocket request passes
   before authentication — including every `/api/*` call the SPA
   makes after the shell loads. The request `Host` must be loopback
   **or** match a `trustedHosts` entry (exact on `host:port`, any port
   on a port-less entry); an attached `Origin` must equal that `Host`;
   `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` is refused. A failed Host check
   returns **403 `forbidden`**; a trusted-but-unauthenticated request
   returns **401 `unauthorized`**. The root `GET /` is the token
   redemption route and is answered by layer 1 first, so a forged Host
   there reads **401, not 403** — the fence is only observable on
   `/api/*`.

The entrypoint parses the token from the readiness line and writes it
to `$DSH_HOME/web-token` (on the `dsh` volume, so a fresh
`charly update` rebuild re-captures it). In-box probes authenticate
with the token, e.g.
`curl "http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=$(cat $DSH_HOME/web-token)"`.

## Reaching the web UI through a reverse proxy (e.g. Tailscale)

Because the app binds loopback only, every off-loopback route is a
reverse proxy in front of it (`tailscale serve`, an SSH `-L` tunnel,
an ingress). Such a proxy forwards `Host: <proxy-authority>` — which
is **neither loopback nor in `trustedHosts`** by default — so the
shell loads (`/` → 200) but every `/api/*` call returns **403
forbidden** and the SPA renders an "authentication required" / dead
page. **`GET /` returning 200 does NOT prove the web UI works; always
exercise an `/api/*` request.**

The fix is the repeatable `--trusted-host <authority>` flag
(`dsh web --trusted-host <proxy-host>:<port>`). Note `lanAddresses`
is only populated when the bind host is `0.0.0.0`, which `dsh web`
deliberately is not — so when bound to loopback, only the explicit
`--trusted-host` entries are trusted. Pass the proxy authority, e.g.:

```bash
# expose the loopback web UI on the tailnet, 1:1, and trust its authority
dsh --profile web --port 3080 --trusted-host "$(tailscale status --self --json \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["Self"]["DNSName"].rstrip("."))'):3080"
tailscale serve --bg --https=3080 http://127.0.0.1:3080   # 1:1; NOT 443
```

**The exposed URL contract — `https://` and a token.** `--https=3080`
installs an **HTTPS-only** listener (there is no HTTP one), so a plain
`http://<self>.ts.net:3080/` is answered by that TLS server with
**`400 Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server.`** Use
`https://`. And because `dsh web` authenticates every request, the bare
`https://<self>.ts.net:3080/` returns **401** — the URL must carry the
launch token, which redeems it (`303`) and sets the authority-scoped
cookie. Both together:

```bash
# the working URL (token from the durable file the entrypoint writes)
https://<self>.ts.net:3080/?token=$(cat ~/.dsh/web-token)
# or: ~/.local/bin/dsh-web-url [--local|--tailnet] [--open]
```

On a **pod**, the socat forwarder is what makes the published port
loopback-reaching, so a browser hitting `127.0.0.1:<published>` stays
on the trusted loopback authority. A pod reached through any
off-loopback proxy needs the same `--trusted-host` treatment: set the
`dsh-web` candy's `DSH_WEB_TRUSTED_HOSTS` to the proxy authority
(`host:port`, space- or comma-separated) and the entrypoint forwards
each as `--trusted-host`.

## Usage

```yaml
# charly.yml
my-web-box:
  candy:
    - dsh-web   # CLI + web UI
my-tui-box:
  candy:
    - dsh-tui   # CLI + terminal UI
```

## Plugins and experimental features (the Plugins page)

Agent Teams, Auto Authorization Review, Automation tasks, and Voice
input are **package-bundles**: each is a name in a profile's
`dsh.profile.bundles` (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/package.json`). The
Web sidebar's Plugins page toggles one by writing a `disabled:`
override into that profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — not by editing the
bundle list. **Composition is not activation:** `--dump-config` shows
a bundle was composed; only a boot proves it activated. Check both:

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -E 'agent-team|auto-review|ui-schedule|ui-voice-input'
dsh --profile web --port 13080 --no-open   # a failed plugin prints "N entries did not activate: <reason>"
```

| Feature | Bundle | web | dsh-tui |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent Teams | `dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` | ✅ | ❌ |
| Auto review | `dsh-experimental-auto-review` | ✅ | ❌ |
| Automation tasks | `dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` | ✅ | ❌ |
| Voice input | `dsh-experimental-voice-input-bundle` | ✅ (needs a model) | ❌ |
| git-worktree (community) | `dsh-git-worktree` | ✅ | ❌ |
| OpenCharly (native) | `dsh-opencharly` | ✅ | ❌ |

The `dsh-web` profile ships **eight** bundles: `dsh-base`, `dsh-web-app`,
the four experimental features, the community `dsh-git-worktree`
plugin, and the native `dsh-opencharly` plugin.
Both plugins are VENDORED PREBUILT as tarballs under
`candy/dsh-web/web-profile/vendor-tgz/` and consumed as `file:` deps, so
the profile install resolves them OFFLINE (no codeload fetch, no
per-dep npm-install bootstrap — the flake `pod-dsh#26` recorded).
Each tarball's source repo+commit and SHA-256 are recorded in
`vendor-tgz/README.md`, with the two hashes in
`vendor-tgz/SHA256SUMS` (verified in the volume by the bed).
`dsh-opencharly` is server-only (no browser client); the other ships a
`lib/client.js` browser half. Both are installed at image BUILD time
into `~/.local/share/dsh/profile-home` and seeded into the `dsh` volume
by the entrypoint — because profile bundles resolve from
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/node_modules`, which the named volume shadows.

- **Agent Teams** runs in `web`/`headless`: the Lead spawns named
  teammates, exchanges durable messages, and uses a shared task board.
  It needs durable session storage (`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`,
  in `dsh-base`) and is **durable but PROCESS-LOCAL** — all members
  share ONE working directory (no worktree isolation), and there is no
  cross-process/cross-client team.
- **Voice input** activates but needs a one-time **241 MB** local
  SenseVoice model that `dsh` does NOT pre-fetch — the mic appears,
  and recognition fails until it is prepared. In the UI click
  *Download and prepare*; to pre-seed (sizes + sha256 are pinned in the
  package's `runtime/assets.json`), place the verified files under
  `$DSH_HOME/speech-to-text/sensevoice/models/`:
  `sensevoice-onnx/model.int8.onnx` (239233841 B), `sensevoice-onnx/tokens.txt`
  (315894 B), `silero/silero_vad.onnx` (1807522 B).
- **The `dsh-tui` profile cannot host these bundles.** The dsh-TUI
  adapter rejects the root capabilities they require —
  `Error: dsh-tui: root.effect is unavailable from a plugin activation`
  — so adding them to the `dsh-tui` profile makes them FAIL to
  activate (`N entries did not activate`). Keep that profile at
  `dsh-base` + `dsh-tui`. The dsh-TUI launcher is standalone (it has
  no remote/attach), so there is **no** Agent-Teams coordination
  between the TUI and the web GUI: team coordination is within one
  Web/headless process, not across the two UIs.

The `dsh-web` candy **stages the enabled profile** into the `dsh`
volume at deploy time (a `data:` entry → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web`), so
a freshly deployed pod has all eight bundles composed without any
in-UI toggling. The `dsh-tui` candy keeps its profile at base + the
plugin. This is composition, not activation: the web UI's own boot
proves they activate (a failed one prints `N entries did not
activate`).
